core_obligations: Identify the multiplicative subset (proof lines 728-733): let S be the set of elements of A mapping to invertible elements of the ring of sections of Z, which is the localization of A/I at f.

Characterize the primes of the localization (proof lines 733-742): if a prime p does not specialize to Z then p generates the unit ideal in A/I localized at f, so f^n = g + h with g in p and h in I, whence g in S and p is not in the spectrum of S^{-1}A; conversely if p specializes to Z through a prime q containing I with f not in q then S^{-1}A maps to A_q and p survives; this proves (1).

Conclude the remaining statements (proof lines 744-747): the isomorphism class of the localization depends only on the subset it defines, which gives (2); the map S^{-1}A -> (A/I)_f is surjective by construction, which gives (3); and for a ring map with a locally closed subscheme Z' mapping into Z the corresponding multiplicative subset contains the image of S, which gives the final uniqueness statement.
proof_roadmap: Define the multiplicative subset through invertibility of the sections on Z.
Characterize the primes surviving in the localization by an explicit divisibility argument.
Read off dependence only on the subset, the closed subscheme structure and the functoriality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a locally closed subscheme Z of the spectrum of A of the form D(f) cap V(I) there is a multiplicative subset S such that the spectrum of S^{-1}A is homeomorphic to the set of points specializing to Z, that this algebra depends only on the underlying subset, that Z is a closed subscheme of it, and that ring maps with a compatible Z' induce a unique map of these localizations (statement lines 709-726). The proof (proof lines 728-748) identifies S through the sections on Z, characterizes the surviving primes by an explicit divisibility argument, and derives the remaining statements formally. H2: one explicit argument with two inputs, written out in full.
